Do I need travel insurance for Koh Samui? | It isn't required for visa-exempt tourists, but it is essential in practice. Thai hospitals ask for an insurer's guarantee or a deposit before treatment, and a scooter crash or evacuation to Bangkok can cost far more than most people can pay.
~Does travel insurance cover scooter accidents in Thailand? | Only if you meet the policy's conditions, which usually means a full motorcycle licence at home plus an International Driving Permit with the motorcycle category, a helmet, no alcohol and an engine within the policy's limit (often 125 cc). Without them, claims are commonly refused.
Will a hospital on Koh Samui treat me without insurance? | Emergency departments will stabilise you, but private hospitals expect a deposit or full payment by card or cash before admission, surgery or discharge. The government Koh Samui Hospital near Nathon is much cheaper for minor problems.
Does my insurance cover diving on Koh Samui? | Many policies cover recreational diving only to a set depth and within your certification level, and some exclude it entirely. Check the depth limit and whether decompression treatment in a recompression chamber is included before you dive.
Am I covered on a jet ski? | Often not, or only for your own injuries. Many policies exclude jet skis or your liability for damage to the craft, so check the water-sports list and never leave your passport with a jet-ski operator.
What if my boat trip is cancelled for weather? | On our tours you choose a full refund or a new date, so there is nothing to claim. Ang Thong Marine Park's yearly closure from 1 November to 15 December is scheduled, so it isn't covered as a surprise.
How do I get a police report for an insurance claim? | Call the Tourist Police on 1155 or go to the police station for the area where it happened, with your passport, a list of items and values, and any evidence. Ask for the report in English or with an English summary, and make it within 24 hours.
Does travel insurance cover the Destination Thailand Visa? | The DTV doesn't normally require insurance on the standard embassy list, but a holiday policy may not cover stays of up to 180 days. Long-stayers usually need an annual expat health policy instead.
Which Thai visas require health insurance? | The Long-Term Resident visa needs cover of at least USD 50,000 (or Thai social security, or USD 100,000 held in a bank for 12 months), and the Non-Immigrant O-A retirement visa needs health insurance meeting the embassy's minimum. Visa-exempt stays and tourist visas don't.
Is dental treatment covered by travel insurance? | Usually only emergency pain relief up to a low limit. Planned work such as crowns or implants is almost never covered, so ask your insurer before treatment and keep itemised receipts.
